text: CHAPTER 30
speaker: Narrator

text: The End of Choosing
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The City stopped pretending to be passive.
speaker: Narrator

text: It began with the water.
speaker: Narrator

text: They had grown used to the shallow black pools that appeared in chambers and along corridors—one more unpleasant feature of a place that seemed to hold a personal grudge against human comfort. Then the water started moving with intent.
speaker: Narrator

text: When Balag knelt to refill a waterskin, the surface rippled toward him before he touched it. Small, deliberate rings traveled uphill against the natural slope of the stone. He froze with the skin still in his hand.
speaker: Narrator

text: Did you see that?
speaker: Balag

text: Ninsun had already turned.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Yes.
speaker: Ninsun

text: It moved.
speaker: Balag

text: Water does that.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Not toward a man before he touches it.
speaker: Balag

text: No one answered.
speaker: Narrator

text: They pressed on, keeping clear of the black pools. A few minutes later Balag muttered under his breath about the City, the dead, and the questionable intelligence of anyone who walked willingly into a place that had been buried for thousands of years. His voice was low, barely more than breath.
speaker: Narrator

text: It carried strangely down the corridor.
speaker: Narrator

text: A moment later it came back.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not as an echo. The voice was stretched thin and wet, distorted in a way that made Zik's skin crawl, but the words were unmistakably Balag's, and they came from somewhere ahead.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag stopped walking.
speaker: Narrator

text: A second repetition rose from behind. A third bled out of the darkness to their left.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun stepped toward the nearest wall and held her palm just short of the oily stone.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: It's recording us. Or learning how we sound when we're afraid.
speaker: Ninsun

text: I wasn't afraid,
speaker: Balag

text: Balag said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The wall repeated him, word for word, in a voice that had learned his cadence better than he liked.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu laughed once, short and without humor.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The City disagrees.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Behind them the water rippled again—and this time it spoke in Zik's voice.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu.
speaker: Zik
note: CITY MIMIC of Zik's voice from the water: wet, stretched, wrong.

text: She spun. Nothing stood behind her. The black surface trembled once and went still. The mark under Zik's wrappings gave a slow, answering pulse.
speaker: Narrator

text: He did not like that the City had borrowed his voice. He liked even less that it had known exactly whose name to say with it.
speaker: Narrator

text: They moved faster after that.
speaker: Narrator

text: The statues came next.
speaker: Narrator

text: The first stood at the mouth of a side passage they had not noticed before. It was taller than any of them, carved from the same dull, oily stone as the walls, its face blank except for the spiral-drop symbol cut deep into the brow. It did not move when they approached. It simply occupied the space with the absolute patience of something that had nowhere else to be.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik tested the floor in front of it out of habit. His body still knew the sequence even if the conscious lesson was gone. The stone held.
speaker: Narrator

text: They passed it.
speaker: Narrator

text: When Zik looked back, the statue had turned its head to watch them leave.
speaker: Narrator

text: No one commented. Commenting would have required deciding what the movement meant.
speaker: Narrator

text: The second statue waited at a junction three turns later. The third appeared in a doorway that had been empty when they last checked. By the fourth they had stopped counting.
speaker: Narrator

text: The City was no longer content to wait behind thresholds. It was rearranging the board.
speaker: Narrator

text: They made camp in a chamber that offered two exits and no pools. Balag took first watch. Ninsun wrote until the stylus refused another line and then sat staring at the blank space as though the parchment itself had begun to withhold cooperation. Enhedu sat with her back to the wall, the figurine in her lap, looking at it the way a person studies an object whose purpose belongs to someone else.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik opened the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: The map had shifted again. The upper layers—the desert, the outpost, the first staircase—had faded almost to invisibility. In their place the ink had thickened into a denser network of descending lines. At the center of the densest tangle the spiral-drop appeared complete, larger than any they had seen.
speaker: Narrator

text: Beneath it, in a hand that was neither his father's nor his own:
speaker: Narrator

text: THE CITY IS TIRED OF WAITING.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: He closed the book before anyone else could see the words.
speaker: Narrator

text: Sometime after the others had gone quiet he heard water moving in the dark. When he opened his eyes the statue was standing in the entrance, taller than the doorway, its head forced down beneath the stone arch to fit. The spiral-drop crown sat on its brow. Its carved face pointed straight at him.
speaker: Narrator

text: It did not attack.
speaker: Narrator

text: It waited.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik's hand went to his knife. The statue did not shift. He looked past it to the doorway, then back at the stone face, then down at the mark on his palm. The mark knocked once, soft and deliberate, against the inside of his skin.
speaker: Narrator
